notes: The catalog covers the 33 recruitable units in the 2.0.0.5.2340 Standard Versus data extracted by mechcore. Later builds and mode-specific or summoned units can contain additional IDs.

Unit cost and unlockCost are base supply charges, before specialist, card, or other discounts. A zero unlock price is omitted by the source exporter and restored here. Tier groups units for analysis. Overlord costs 500 supply and belongs to tier 400.

Footprints estimate board occupancy using each squad’s extracted formation card width and depth in metres. The height field represents board depth. These dimensions approximate occupied space and do not describe collision bounds.

Range is the extracted main attack range in metres, including internal melee ranges. Speed is base movement speed in metres per second. Domain and targeting describe the unmodified unit and its main attack. Secondary weapons and technology can change effective targeting and range.

Roles and addedRoles are Tactibellum heuristics. statModifiers records only verified flat additions to main attack range in metres and speed in metres per second. An empty map leaves other effects unspecified.

Tech costs are base supply before the surcharge for previously researched techs. Legacy-only tech IDs retain their old names with null costs. Other null costs indicate that this catalog has no verified price for the entry.

Specialists includes opening specialists and officer cards because both use officer IDs. Spell and item costs refer to reinforcement acquisition when applicable. Devices, tower skills, and blueprints use their respective action IDs and base supply costs.

The legacy MIT replay parser, the earlier mechstats extraction, and FogMoe’s unit lookup cross-check replay IDs. Balance values use the stated mechcore build. The catalog contains field facts and project-authored tags.

Combat HP and attack values describe one member at level 1. The level rule multiplies HP and damage by levels 1 through 9. Attack is available for verified single-hit main weapons only. An absent combatModifier marks an unmodeled selection. An empty combatModifier marks a verified effect outside stationary HP, damage and cadence. Rates preserve the extracted Q32.32 values.
